strengths: Inference-only, model-agnostic method requiring no retraining; immediately deployable as a drop-in replacement across multiple MDLM architectures
Logarithmic complexity reduction (O(B) → O(log B)) with substantial empirical speedups (up to 10.7×) and consistent improvements (up to 27% on math benchmarks)
Theoretical analysis via Lemmas 1-2 providing formal justification for why DUS achieves joint entropy bounds that confidence-based planners lack
Comprehensive experimental validation across 5 models and 6 benchmarks with proper ablation studies (Section 4.4) validating design choices
Rare speed-quality trade-off where the method achieves both faster inference and better accuracy simultaneously, with clear qualitative examples (Figure 1)
Strong presentation with clear motivation, well-designed figures, and generally accessible writing
weaknesses: Theory-practice gap: Core theoretical analysis assumes fast-mixing first-order Markov chain, but these assumptions are neither empirically validated nor likely to hold for language with known long-range dependencies; no measurement of actual MI decay or verification of spacing bounds in real models
Skip mechanism (Section 3.6) mentioned as important but never formally defined—no threshold values, frequency analysis, or evaluation of how it affects spacing guarantees

Circular reasoning on independence (Eq. 3→4): Paper claims tokens are 'unmasked independently' to justify summing entropies, yet Lemma 2 bounds non-zero MI between tokens; this contradiction needs clarification
Limited baseline comparisons: Only compared against self-confidence in main results; missing comparisons with EB-Sampler, Path Planning (P2), and other recent planners except in limited ablations
Block merging operation (Eq. 7) when |P_R| < |P_{R-1}| could violate claimed spacing guarantees; no analysis of its impact on theoretical bounds

Incomplete mechanism analysis: No sensitivity analysis for dilation base a (only a=2 tested); no investigation of failure modes where method hurts performance (e.g., DiffuCoder-Instruct HumanEval at B=64)
Unjustified connection between entropy minimization and downstream task performance; paper assumes this coupling without explicit justification or alternative objectives comparison
Limited scope: All experiments use semi-AR with blocks B∈{8,16,32,64}; unclear how DUS scales to fully parallel generation, larger blocks, or beyond 7-8B models
Reproducibility gaps: No code release mentioned, skip mechanism thresholds undocumented, model-specific confidence measures not fully detailed

strengths: Strong theoretical foundation grounded in information theory (entropy gap minimization with formal bounds Lemmas 3.3-3.6)
Comprehensive experimental validation across 5 MDLM variants, 4+ benchmarks with consistent improvements (up to 27% on math/code over confidence baseline)
Inference-only method with zero modifications to model training or architecture; broad applicability across diverse models and tasks
Practical value demonstrated through wall-clock speedups (3.9-5.8×) and deterministic, controllable latency via block size B
Thorough ablations and reproducibility support (Appendices B.1-B.9, promised code release) enabling detailed analysis of design choices
Novel position-based (non-model-dependent) scheduling principle orthogonal to adaptive samplers; can enhance EB/CB methods
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figures 1, 4, 5) and qualitative generation trajectories illustrating spacing principle
weaknesses: Theory-practice gap: optimal estimator assumption (Assumption 3.1) doesn't hold for learned denoisers; impact on bound tightness not quantified
VLMC fast-mixing assumption violated on code/reasoning tasks; distinction between full and 'block-level' fast-mixing is informal
Late-iteration analysis relies on heuristic reasoning (richer context helps) rather than formal guarantees; bounds are most informative early only
Inconsistent improvements across tasks: modest gains on general knowledge (BBH +1-5%, MMLU +5-9%) vs. strong gains on math; mechanism unclear
Incomplete baseline comparisons: Path Planning (P2) and Jump Your Steps (JYS) mentioned but not empirically compared; semi-AR block diffusion trade-offs not addressed
Generalization questions: all experiments use semi-AR blocks; single-block (B=G) regime shows low accuracy; scale to 13B+ models untested

Design choices lack principled justification: base a=2 appears arbitrary (Appendix B.4 shows alternatives degrade but no rationale); skip threshold recommendation contradicts ablations (Table 7 shows c=0.3 improves some tasks)
Persistent quality gap to autoregressive models: GSM8K 57% vs 88.5%, HumanEval 11.6% vs 61.6%, limiting practical deployment scenarios
Hybrid extension (Section 4.4) orthogonal to main method; improvements come with NFE cost tradeoff, not clearly separable from adaptive samplers
Limited scope: tested on 7-8B parameter models only; applicability to different MDLM architectures beyond LLaDA/Dream/DiffuCoder unclear
